title: Model Collapse — Cambridge IIB research presentation

textRun.content: How much real text does self-training need?
Synthetic feedback degrades performance or coverage of the original distribution.
PPL = exp[ mean(−log p(true next token)) ]
Higher perplexity means more surprise at held-out real text.
Real-data controls help us interpret why it rises.
Repeated exposure improves the training fit while held-out prediction worsens.
Full y-axis (0–360). Same real test after each cycle. Mixture detail follows.
Fresh real data slightly improves real-text prediction.
Recursive synthetic targets cause much larger deterioration.
A small real fraction can strongly reduce the damage here.
Open question: how much of the late flattening survives a constant learning rate?
One seed, ten cycles, declining LR and some GPU differences.
Next: constant LR, longer trajectories and multiple seeds.
